cutoff: Research cutoff: October 17, 2026, 6:33 a.m. CT (11:33 UTC). Weekend edition: equity, ETF, VIX and Treasury observations are October 16 prior-session; funding fixings are October 15. No live executable liquidity was verified.

stories.head: Meta releases Muse Spark Open; deployment scale still matters
stories.alt: Three specification panels show 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active parameters per token and a one-million-token context window; a note distinguishes active compute from total weight memory.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Meta AI Research release, October 15, 2026. Company-reported specifications, not independent benchmarks.
stories.fact: Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open on October 15: 816 billion total parameters, 42 billion active and a one-million-token context window. The release uses the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms.
stories.inference: Open weights expand deployment choices, while total model memory remains a separate constraint from active computation.
stories.uncertainty: Vendor capability claims do not establish MATLAB coding accuracy, trading suitability or performance on a particular workstation.
stories.why: Evaluate a small, isolated coding workflow for correctness, memory, latency, data permissions and license terms before choosing hosted or local deployment.

stories.head: Earnings-call research exposes within-event timing leakage
stories.alt: A conceptual availability contract links input boundaries, evidence of completion plus processing time, and an outcome window that starts after usable input; the authors’ baseline changed 9.4% of return signs.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Ma et al., arXiv:2610.21659v1, submitted October 15, 2026. Conceptual sequence, not a calibrated timeline.
stories.fact: Ma and coauthors examine 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. Moving the outcome start from a call-start proxy to a completion proxy changes 9.4% of return signs in their baseline, with the return endpoint held fixed. Their Availability Contract makes input and outcome clocks explicit.
stories.inference: Chronological train/test splits alone cannot remove leakage when a target begins before an event’s model input is complete.
stories.uncertainty: Completion is reconstructed from audio plus a stipulated processing allowance; timing evidence and benchmark design limit generalization.
stories.why: Timestamp transcript/audio completion, processing and order eligibility separately; compare event labels under alternative availability allowances before retraining.

stories.head: Friday’s tech-led decline leaves Nasdaq down 2.1%
stories.alt: Zero-referenced horizontal bars show October 16 closing declines of 0.3% for the Dow, 1.1% for the S&P 500, 1.7% for the Russell 2000 and 2.1% for the Nasdaq Composite.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Associated Press, October 16, 2026 closing summary. Rounded cash-index returns.
stories.fact: U.S. stocks closed lower Friday: S&P 500 −1.1%, Nasdaq Composite −2.1%, Dow −0.3% and Russell 2000 −1.7%. Technology weakness weighed on the session.
stories.inference: A single broad-index exposure can conceal materially different sector and small-cap risk.
stories.uncertainty: Cash-index returns are not SPY/QQQ returns, executable quotes or proof of a specific dealer-positioning mechanism.
stories.why: Rebuild Monday’s quote and auction baseline from fresh observations; do not carry Friday’s spread or expiry assumptions into new orders.

stories.head: September import prices rise 1.1%, including nonfuel pressure
stories.alt: Zero-based bars show September monthly import and export price changes: all imports +1.1%, fuel imports +4.8%, nonfuel imports +0.7% and all exports +2.2%; figures are not seasonally adjusted.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; BLS October 16, 2026 release, September reference month. Overlapping categories are not additive.
stories.fact: BLS reported September import prices up 1.1% monthly and 8.1% annually. Fuel imports rose 4.8% monthly and nonfuel imports 0.7%; export prices rose 2.2%. These indexes are not seasonally adjusted.
stories.inference: Inflation research should separate fuel shocks from broader imported-input pressure.
stories.uncertainty: Import/export indexes are not CPI or PCE; revisions, currency effects, margins and uncertain pass-through limit policy conclusions.
stories.why: Keep the 7:30 a.m. CT October 16 release vintage and test the incremental information in nonfuel prices rather than treating the headline as a direct Fed signal.

stories.head: Travelers’ earnings show why per-share growth needs decomposition
stories.alt: Grouped zero-based bars compare Travelers’ third-quarter diluted EPS in 2025 and 2026: GAAP $8.24 versus $9.04 and non-GAAP core $8.14 versus $9.18; a caption contrasts core-income and share-count changes.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Travelers earnings release, October 16, 2026. Q3 2025 versus Q3 2026; core EPS is non-GAAP.
stories.fact: Travelers reported Q3 net income of $1.917 billion and core income of $1.947 billion. Core income increased 4%, while core EPS increased 13% to $9.18; diluted average shares declined 7%. Higher reserve development and investment income were partly offset by catastrophe losses.
stories.inference: Share repurchases and reserve movements can make EPS growth look stronger than growth in total underlying earnings.
stories.uncertainty: Core income is company-defined non-GAAP, reserve estimates can change, and catastrophe losses remain volatile.
stories.why: Decompose earnings into total income, share count, investment yield, reserve development and underwriting performance before scoring an earnings surprise.
